canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.name: Choy sum soup with minced pork
aliases: Choy sum and minced pork soup
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.serving_basis: About three bowls of clear soup for a family meal.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.description: Tender choy sum cooks briefly in a light broth with loose pieces of minced pork and scallion. This familiar soup is quick to prepare and pairs well with steamed rice.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.finished_dish: A clear, mild broth with tender pork and bright green choy sum that is cooked just until done.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.excerpt: A clear, mild broth with tender pork and bright green choy sum that is cooked just until done.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice; it pairs well with braised fish or another simple main dish.
tips: Stir gently when adding the pork to boiling water so it separates into small pieces.
Add the greens when the broth is boiling and cook for only 2–3 minutes to prevent them from becoming too soft.
Season with fish sauce a little at a time near the end.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.tip: Stir gently when adding the pork to boiling water so it separates into small pieces.
search_terms: Choy sum soup with minced pork
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.image_alt: Choy sum soup with minced pork in a white ceramic bowl; original Bếp Việt dish artwork.
preparation_steps: Trim any wilted leaves and wash the choy sum well. Cut into bite-sized lengths and drain.
Make sure the ground pork is ready and drain off excess moisture. Crush or mince the scallion roots.
Chop the scallion leaves and set aside to garnish the soup.
cooking_steps: Bring the water to a boil. Add the oil, crushed scallion root and minced pork, stirring gently to separate the meat.
When the broth returns to a boil, skim the surface and add the choy sum.
Season with fish sauce, salt, sugar and optional monosodium glutamate. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the greens are just tender, taste and turn off the heat.
Finish with ground pepper and scallion. Avoid overcooking to keep the greens bright and lightly crisp.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.time_note: Estimated preparation and cooking time; cook the greens only until tender to retain their color and texture.

hu-tieu-my-tho.name: My Tho-style hu tieu noodle soup
aliases: My Tho shrimp and meat noodle soup
hu-tieu-my-tho.serving_basis: Four bowls of hu tieu with springy rice noodles, clear pork broth, pork and shrimp.
hu-tieu-my-tho.description: Small, chewy and crispy rice noodles in sweet pork bone broth, fragrant with dried shrimp; Served with pork, shrimp and chive sprouts.
hu-tieu-my-tho.finished_dish: A bowl of My Tho hu tieu with springy rice noodles, clear pork-and-dried-shrimp broth, pork, fresh shrimp, bean sprouts and garlic chives.
hu-tieu-my-tho.serving: Serve hot with bean sprouts, garlic chives, lime and chili on the side. Enjoy as soup or serve the broth separately for a dry-style bowl.
hu-tieu-my-tho.image_alt: My Tho hu tieu with rice noodles, pork, shrimp, bean sprouts and garlic chives in a blue-and-white ceramic bowl.
hu-tieu-my-tho.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Skim regularly and keep the broth at a gentle simmer for clarity.
Lightly toast the shrimp shells, dried shrimp and dried squid to deepen the aroma without overpowering the pork broth.
Blanch the noodles just before serving to keep them springy.
preparation_steps: Blanch and rinse the pork bones. Rinse the dried shrimp and squid, soak until soft, then drain.
Rinse and peel the shrimp, removing the veins; reserve the shells to toast for the broth. Simmer the pork shoulder until just cooked, cool, then slice.
Rinse the bean sprouts, garlic chives and scallions; cut the chives into short lengths. Mince the shallots and garlic.
cooking_steps: Simmer the bones in water over low heat for about 60 minutes, skimming often. Toast the shrimp shells, dried shrimp and dried squid until fragrant; place them in a filter bag or add them for the final 20 minutes, then remove.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Quickly stir-fry the shrimp until just pink, season lightly and set aside. Season the broth with fish sauce, salt, rock sugar and pepper.
Blanch the noodles according to the package directions and divide among bowls with the bean sprouts, chives, pork and shrimp.
Ladle over the hot broth, add scallions and fried shallots, and serve with lime and chili to taste.

banh-canh-nam-pho.name: Nam Pho thick rice noodle soup
banh-canh-nam-pho.serving_basis: Four bowls of chewy rice noodles with shrimp-pork cakes in lightly thickened crab and shrimp broth.
banh-canh-nam-pho.description: The rice noodle soup mixed with tapioca starch is soft and flexible, nestled in a light, naturally orange-red crab and shrimp broth; The cake bowl has shrimp and meat patties, green onions and pepper.
banh-canh-nam-pho.finished_dish: A bowl of Nam Pho noodle soup with lightly thickened crab and shrimp broth, naturally orange-red from crab roe and annatto oil, chewy noodles and fragrant shrimp-pork cakes.
banh-canh-nam-pho.serving: Serve hot with scallions, cilantro and pepper; add fresh chili if desired. Keep the broth lightly thickened so the chewy noodles remain distinct.
banh-canh-nam-pho.image_alt: Nam Pho noodle soup with chewy rice noodles, shrimp-pork cakes and thick orange-red broth in a white ceramic bowl.
banh-canh-nam-pho.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Toast the shrimp shells before simmering them with the bones for a naturally sweet, aromatic broth.
Cook the crab liquid over medium heat and stir gently so the roe sets into delicate clusters.
Add the noodles near the end so they stay chewy and the broth thickens lightly without turning pasty.

ingredients.name: Fresh thick rice noodles made from rice

preparation_steps: Blanch and rinse the pork bones. Peel and devein the shrimp, reserving the shells for the broth. Chop the shrimp and mix with pork paste, pepper and a little fish sauce.
Finely dice the pork belly. Mince the shallots and garlic; rinse and chop the scallions and cilantro. If using fresh noodles, gently separate the strands before cooking.
Pound or blend the crab with a little water and strain it through a sieve; reserve the roe separately. Rinse the picked crab meat.
cooking_steps: Simmer the bones in 2 litres of water for about 40 minutes, skimming the surface. Toast the shrimp shells until fragrant, add them for the final 15 minutes, then remove.

Cook the crab liquid over medium heat, stirring gently until the roe sets, then lift it out. Sauté the shallots in annatto oil, stir-fry the pork belly and crab roe, then add the shrimp, crab meat and small portions of the beaten pork paste.
Combine the crab liquid with the bone broth and season with fish sauce, salt and sugar. Add small shrimp-pork cakes and cook through, then return the crab roe to the pot.
Add the noodles and cook until tender and chewy and the broth thickens lightly. If using dried noodles, soak or blanch them according to the package directions first.
Adjust the seasoning, turn off the heat and add scallions, cilantro and pepper. Ladle into bowls and serve hot with chili to taste.

bun-nuoc-leo-soc-trang.name: Soc Trang bun nuoc leo
aliases: Vermicelli noodle soup with beef sauce
bun-nuoc-leo-soc-trang.serving_basis: Four bowls of bun nuoc leo with fish, shrimp and fresh Mekong Delta vegetables.
bun-nuoc-leo-soc-trang.description: The beef fish sauce broth is fragrant with lemongrass and coconut water, served over fresh vermicelli with snakehead fish, shrimp, eggplant and vegetables.
bun-nuoc-leo-soc-trang.finished_dish: A bowl of Soc Trang bun nuoc leo with a fragrant prahok, lemongrass and coconut broth, sweet snakehead fish and shrimp, tender eggplant and crisp fresh vegetables.
bun-nuoc-leo-soc-trang.serving: Serve hot with bean sprouts, banana blossom and shredded water spinach. Taste the broth first, then add chili and lime as desired.
bun-nuoc-leo-soc-trang.image_alt: Soc Trang bun nuoc leo with snakehead fish, shrimp, eggplant and fresh vegetables in a blue-and-white ceramic bowl.
bun-nuoc-leo-soc-trang.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Strain the prahok broth several times to remove bones and keep it smooth.
Add salt only after combining the paste with the bone broth, since saltiness varies by brand and type.
Cook the eggplant until just tender and blanch the noodles separately to preserve their texture.
preparation_steps: Blanch and rinse the pork bones. Rinse the fish and shrimp; cut the fish into serving pieces and devein the shrimp.
Mix the prahok with water and simmer gently until the fish breaks down, then strain thoroughly to remove bones. Bruise the lemongrass and mince the shallots and garlic.
Cut the eggplant into chunks, soak briefly in lightly salted water, then drain. Rinse the bean sprouts, banana blossom and shredded water spinach.
cooking_steps: Simmer the bones with water and lemongrass for 45–50 minutes, skimming the surface. Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant, add the strained prahok and coconut water, warm gently, then stir into the bone broth.
Season gradually with sugar and salt. Add the eggplant and cook until just tender; keep the broth hot over low heat.
Poach the fish until just cooked and the shrimp until pink; remove without breaking them up. Blanch the noodles separately and divide among bowls.
Arrange the fish, shrimp and scallions over the noodles, then ladle in the broth. Serve with bean sprouts, banana blossom, water spinach, lime and chili.

keywords: Vermicelli noodle soup with beef sauce

banh-hoi-long-heo-binh-dinh.name: Binh Dinh banh hoi with pork offal
aliases: Binh Dinh pork belly porridge cake
banh-hoi-long-heo-binh-dinh.serving_basis: Four servings of banh hoi and pork offal with fresh herbs, cucumber and sweet-and-sour fish sauce.
banh-hoi-long-heo-binh-dinh.description: Soft white rice cake sprinkled with onion fat and served with boiled meat, pork intestines, herbs and a bowl of garlic and chili fish sauce with a strong earthy flavor.
banh-hoi-long-heo-binh-dinh.finished_dish: A platter of Binh Dinh banh hoi with soft rice vermicelli sheets brushed with scallion oil, just-cooked pork and offal, fresh herbs and garlic-chili dipping sauce.
banh-hoi-long-heo-binh-dinh.serving: Arrange the vermicelli and pork offal in separate groups. Wrap with fresh herbs and cucumber, then dip in the seasoned fish sauce.
banh-hoi-long-heo-binh-dinh.image_alt: Binh Dinh banh hoi with scallion-oil vermicelli sheets, boiled pork and offal, fresh herbs and a bowl of fish sauce.
banh-hoi-long-heo-binh-dinh.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Clean the offal thoroughly and use fresh boiling water for each type to keep the flavours clean.
Cook the liver and intestines just until done so they remain tender rather than dry or chewy.
Brush the scallion oil over the vermicelli while it is warm so it stays fragrant and moist.
preparation_steps: Rub the intestines several times with salt and lime, then rinse well. Rinse the liver, heart and pork; bruise the ginger.
Finely slice the scallions and rinse the herbs, lettuce and cucumber. Mince the garlic and chili for the dipping sauce.
Rehydrate the banh hoi according to the package directions and separate it into serving portions.
cooking_steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil with ginger and a little salt. Cook the pork belly until done and remove it. Cook the heart, liver and intestines separately just until cooked through. Let them cool slightly, then slice.
Heat the oil and pour it over the scallions to make scallion oil. Mix fish sauce with warm water, lime and sugar; add garlic and chili, then balance the sweet, sour and salty flavours.
Steam or briefly blanch the banh hoi until soft and warm, arrange on a platter and brush with scallion oil. Serve with the pork offal, boiled pork, fresh herbs and cucumber.
Wrap the banh hoi with herbs and pork, then dip in the garlic-chili fish sauce.
